questions.question: A categorical rating factor labels three unordered regions by 1,2,3. An analyst puts the label directly into a linear log-rate predictor with one coefficient. What extra restriction does this impose compared with separate category indicators?
options: Equal fitted rates in all three regions.
Equal log-rate increments between successive labels.
A rate in region three exactly three times that in region one.
A separate unconstrained rate for each region.

questions.question: A factor has categories L,M,H. A log-rate model includes an intercept and indicators $I_M=\mathbf1_{\{M\}}$, $I_H=\mathbf1_{\{H\}}$, using L as reference. Which indicator values represent L?
Binary rating indicators A,B enter $\log\lambda=\beta_0+\beta_AA+\beta_BB+\beta_{AB}AB$, where $\lambda$ is the fitted claim rate. In which group is the interaction term $\beta_{AB}AB$ active?
options: Only the group with A=1 and B=1.
Every group with A=1 or B=1.
Only groups with A and B different.
Every group with equal A and B.

questions.question: A binary-factor model has $\log\lambda=\beta_0+\beta_AA+\beta_BB$ with no interaction, and $\lambda_{ab}$ is its fitted rate at $A=a,B=b$. Which quantity must be the same across the two B groups for every real coefficient vector?
options: The realised claim count in every policy.

questions.question: An observational insurance GLM fits a lower claim rate for one vehicle category after controlling for its included rating factors. Does this establish that changing a policyholder’s vehicle to that category will reduce their claim rate?
options: Yes; controlling included factors eliminates every other possible explanation.
Yes; a log link turns a fitted association into an intervention effect.
No; a fitted GLM cannot describe any conditional association.
No; a fitted conditional association alone does not establish that causal change.

questions.question: A randomly chosen policy belongs to exactly one rating category L, M or H, with probabilities $P(M)=0.3$ and $P(H)=0.2$. L is the reference category. What is the probability that both non-reference indicators $I_M,I_H$ are zero?
Binary A,B enter $\log\lambda=\beta_0+\beta_AA+\beta_BB+\beta_{AB}AB$. Here $\beta_A=\log1.2$ and $\beta_{AB}=\log1.5$. What is the rate ratio for A=1 versus A=0 at B=1?

A Poisson count model at one policy-year has fitted rate $\lambda=0.1\,1.5^{I_M}2^{I_H}$ for mutually exclusive categories L, M, H, with L as reference. For a policy in H, what is its probability of no claims?

A binary factor A has log-rate coefficient $\beta_A=\log 0.8$ without interactions. Which interpretation of the A=1 versus A=0 contrast is valid for every positive baseline rate, holding other factors fixed?
options: It is 0.8 claims lower per unit exposure.

questions.question: A model has $\lambda_{ab}=0.1\,2^a3^b$ for binary A,B. Compare groups (A,B)=(1,0) and(0,1). What is the first fitted rate divided by the second?

A factor has categories L,M,H with indicators summing to one. A predictor is $\eta=\beta_0+\gamma_LI_L+\gamma_MI_M+\gamma_HI_H$. For a nonzero real c and without constraints, what simultaneous change leaves every fitted predictor unchanged?
options: Add c to $\beta_0$ and add c to each $\gamma$ coefficient.
Add c to $\beta_0$ and subtract c from each $\gamma$ coefficient.
Keep $\beta_0$ and add c to each $\gamma$ coefficient.
Subtract c from $\beta_0$ and keep each $\gamma$ coefficient.

questions.question: A binary-factor model uses A=0 as reference and has fitted rate ratio r for A=1 versus A=0, with r>0 and r different from one. It is re-encoded using A=1 as reference without changing either fitted rate. What is the new non-reference multiplier?

For positive fitted rates define $R_A(b)=\lambda_{1 b}/\lambda_{0 b}$ and $R_B(a)=\lambda_{a 1}/\lambda_{a 0}$. In $\log\lambda=\beta_0+\beta_AA+\beta_BB+\beta_{AB}AB$, which relation is valid for every real coefficient vector?

Four positive fitted rates are $\lambda_{00}=0.1$, $\lambda_{10}=0.2$, $\lambda_{01}=0.3$, $\lambda_{11}=0.9$. In a binary log-rate model, what is the interaction multiplier $\mathrm{e}^{\beta_{AB}}$?

A model is $\log\lambda=\beta_0+\beta_AA+\beta_BB+\beta_{AB}AB$. Recode A by C=1−A while keeping B unchanged. Which identity for the coefficient of B preserves fitted rates for every choice of the original coefficients in $\log\lambda=\alpha_0+\alpha_CC+\alpha_BB+\alpha_{CB}CB$?

Two policies differ only in binary rating factor A and exposure. With no interactions, the A=1 rate is 1.5 times the A=0 rate. Exposures are two years for A=1 and one year for A=0. What is the ratio of their expected claim counts?

A binary log-rate model has coefficients $\beta_0,\beta_A,\beta_B,\beta_{AB}$. The observed rating groups are only(A,B)=(0,0) and(1,1); both occur, but the crossed groups do not. Which part of the three factor coefficients is identifiable from these group means alone?
options: Each of the three coefficients separately.

questions.question: A binary log-rate model is $\log\lambda=\beta_0+\beta_AA+\beta_BB+\beta_{AB}AB$. Recode both factors as $C=1-A$ and $D=1-B$, and write the equivalent predictor as $\alpha_0+\alpha_CC+\alpha_DD+\alpha_{CD}CD$. Which identity for the interaction coefficient preserves every cell rate for every original coefficient vector?

An interaction-free model gives rates 0.1,0.5 for A=0 at B=0,1, and rates 0.12,0.6 for A=1. Among A=0 policies,90% have B=1; among A=1 policies,10% have B=1. All policies have equal exposure. Which marginal comparison follows?
options: A=1 has higher average rate 0.552 versus 0.14 because its within-B multiplier is 1.2.
A=1 has lower average rate 0.168 versus 0.46 despite a higher rate at either B.
Both groups have the same average rate 0.36 because there is no interaction.
The average A=1 rate must be 1.2 times the average A=0 rate.

questions.question: A binary log-rate model has main coefficient $\beta_A=\log1.2$. The A=1 versus A=0 rate ratio at B=1 is 0.9. What interaction coefficient and direction change are consistent with this fitted model?
options: $\beta_{AB}=\log0.9$; A raises the rate in both B groups.
$\beta_{AB}=\log1.08$; A lowers the rate in both B groups.
$\beta_{AB}=\log(4/3)$; A lowers the rate at B=0 but raises it at B=1.
$\beta_{AB}=\log0.75$; A raises the rate at B=0 but lowers it at B=1.
